Quite the impressive loop this one! I may have tackled it in a particular fit of overconfidence (they do call me the Hike King) because by the one and a half hour mark I was reaching for my white flag. I must clarify that it was my arrogance and no fault of the trail for this state I was in.  It was just then that my humiliation took place. 

I was attempting to make swiftest business of my return to the trail head when I found myself tactfully descending a craggy descent. It was a real one-two of goose step and ole jelly-legs. At mid way into the valley a quiet voice in the distance of my thoughts remarked, 'now if it is true, the old adage, that what goes up must come down, could not also the opposite be true?'

Ignorance may be bliss, but it is frequently short lived. After a good half kilometer ramble in the direction of what I had hoped was home,  I peaked at the ole GPS only to find I was farther from home than I had ever been,  and likely closer to Tobermory than I had certainly planned.  So I shamefully retraced my tired steps and once again ascended crag hill with my tail firmly between my legs. 

Now the trail (or trails) themselves are a terrific array of easy-going gravel walks up to some solid stretches of pock-marked escarpment stone. It's a pretty impressive array and I was generally on my own until I accidentally interrupted a wedding upon my return.  

I should also note,  a good insect repellent is a must,  I tried my best,  and perhaps it was simply that two hour's sweat had washed away some of its effectiveness.  Nevertheless a handful of those buggers found a few hiding places in my person and managed to make some swift withdrawals. I shall call it a donation,  so as to save my dignity,  and expect a write-off when the tax man comes,  so long as I play my cards right.

This trail leads to the beautiful Scotsdale Farm property and leads you through some very picturesque mixed forest. There are quite a few bridges set up to allow for crossing over small creeks and wet spots. The bugs were pretty bad in the forested areas (not just mosquitos, also deer and horse flies near the farm). This section of the Bruce is one of the least maintained, there are a couple of trees down across the path you have to scrabble over, and there are places where golden rod and other y’all herbaceous plants are leaning over the trail. There are also a couple of very rocky points, but nothing too treacherous as this is usually over level ground not going up or down a slope. I wouldn’t bring small children here, but adventurous kids 10 and up can probably handle it, and bigger dogs. There are lots of shorter side trails in silver creek that would be a better bet for people with small kids or dogs that aren’t as surefooted. Saw lots of wildlife including a vibrant red salamander, frogs and chipmunks.

Definitely not an Easy trail. The first 10% is, but everything after that is Moderate...steep bits, rocky bits, and narrow trails with encroaching plant life. Absolutely beautiful and hardly ran into any other people. Went around 6pm on a Saturday.
Great trail. Some sections are overgrown/narrow and some sections are rocky.
It’s a nice trail which has connections to Bruce Trail. I wouldn’t say it is easy though. There are lots of steep and rocky areas and sometimes paths narrow down. We saw a lot of chipmunks.
Great super easy trail for kids. Lots of bugs though so get your bug sprays

Second time for this one just after Scottsdale Farm opened after the Pandemic closure.  Parking lot was pretty full but we only came across a half dozen or so people.  Sunny day but cool wind had me chilled even with a wind breaker on.  Was dry even though we had plenty of rain the last few days.
Good day had by all.
The trail going over Eighth Line is completely closed.

One of the nicest hikes and just less than an hour from Toronto. We did the whole loop. Its definitely a moderate difficulty, some parts are very rocky and slippery. Also many muddy areas, but lots of beauty all along the trail
More then 8.9km

really nice trail. conditions were as expected this time of year - muddy, slushy, icy. only one descent and one ascent that we had to walk off the trail and through brush to get through though. we parked at the eight line and started the loop counter clockwise through Scotsdale Farm. will definitely go back during other seasons as I'm sure it has a lot to offer throughout the year.
Good winter hike. Enough ice on the ground to cause some concern.  Lots of variety and many streams and elevation changes.
great loop, varied path and landscapes, we did it clockwise. lightly frequented.

This is a wonderful trail with diverse terrain. It is more of a moderate hike than easy. There are many different trail heads and options to make the trail shorter or longer. Overall, a very enjoyable experience.
Nice walk/hike through a variety of terrain. Only a portion was rocky.

This trail is moderate as per skill level and it is 9.03km. I used the MapMyWalk app. 
Great walk!
nice trail, but I would not say that it is easy, more like moderate. and way more then 8.9 kms.
overall a really nice trail. easy and clean running clockwise. halfway through gets more rocky and challenging. a couple of nice hills. definitely a nice 9km trail. reccomend it
you will need cleats ideally for the next few weeks. Snow pack and melt run off has turned to sheet ice in many place and it's really hairy.
Great weather yesterday and easy, friendly well marked trail.
Was good. A good mix of forest, open fields,  creeks, and roads. The trail was confusing at 8th line and never did cross the road. Ended up doing a 4.5 km loop.
Flat and boring at the beginning. Get's interesting when you cross south to 27th Sideroad.
I love this trail, hiked it dozens of times and can’t get enough.

Parts of this hike seemed more then an easy trail. But the trail was well marked, took us through a variety of landscapes from riverside to top of valley and everything in between. Easy enough for my eight year old.
good trail, but lots of mosquitoes so come prepared with bug spray

Nice open areas to get a tan and woods
A fair amount of timber cuttings throughout several areas along this trail. Actually opens up trail nicely.
Lots of parking at Scotsdale Farm.   Easy 2 hr hike with some ups, downs and road crossings.  Can be busy.

Easy lightly trafficked trail, pretty flat the whole way although there are some rocky spots deep in the forest (not great footing for people or dogs!) HEAVY mosquitos in late May and some spots of the trail were quite muddy. Overall a nice hike, would do it again.
